indicators.name: Resting heart rate
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Measure after 5 minutes of rest, restrained at your workstation, using the chest-strap or wrist monitor.

actions.green: PLACEHOLDER: Within expected range. Keep up your exercise schedule.
actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure after 10 minutes of rest. Note caffeine, exercise, or stress.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure now. If confirmed, contact the flight surgeon at the next opportunity.

indicators.name: Blood pressure (systolic)
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Seated and restrained, cuff on upper arm at heart level, after 5 minutes of rest.

actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure in 15 minutes. Check hydration and fluid intake.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure now. If confirmed, contact the flight surgeon.

indicators.name: Blood pressure (diastolic)
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Recorded at the same time as systolic.

actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure now. If confirmed, contact the flight surgeon.

indicators.name: Blood glucose (fasting)
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Fingerstick with onboard glucometer before breakfast.

actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Review recent meals and re-test tomorrow morning.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: If low, take fast-acting carbohydrate and re-test in 15 minutes. Contact the flight surgeon.

indicators.name: Body temperature
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Oral or forehead thermometer. Cabin temperature affects readings; note it.

actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure in 1 hour. Note any symptoms.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Possible fever or hypothermia. Contact the flight surgeon and follow the illness procedure.

indicators.name: Sleep duration
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Hours slept in the crew quarters sleep period (wearable or self-report).

actions.green: PLACEHOLDER: Good sleep. Keep your schedule consistent.
actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Dim lights before bed, use eye mask and earplugs, and avoid screens.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Significant sleep loss. Tell the flight surgeon; review workload and fatigue risk.

indicators.name: Mood (self-rated)
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Rate your mood today from 1 (very low) to 5 (very good).

actions.green: PLACEHOLDER: Doing well. Keep in touch with family and crewmates.
actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Take a break, connect with crew or family, and get some exercise.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Talk to a crewmate and book a private conference with the behavioral health team.

indicators.name: Oxygen saturation (SpO₂)
indicators.howToMeasureInSpace: PLACEHOLDER: Fingertip pulse oximeter, hand still and warm.

actions.amber: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure. Check cabin CO₂ and O₂ readings.
actions.red: PLACEHOLDER: Re-measure immediately. If confirmed, notify the crew and the flight surgeon.

bodySystems.name: Heart & circulation
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Fluids shift toward the head; the heart can lose mass and blood volume drops.

bodySystems.name: Bones
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Weight-bearing bones can lose roughly 1–1.5% of mass per month without countermeasures.

bodySystems.name: Muscles
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Postural muscles atrophy without daily resistance exercise.

bodySystems.name: Immune system
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Immune function can change; latent viruses may reactivate.

bodySystems.name: Eyes & vision
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS) can change vision.

bodySystems.name: Mind & behavior
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Isolation, confinement and workload affect mood, cognition and team dynamics.

bodySystems.name: Sleep & circadian rhythm
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: About 16 sunrises a day in low Earth orbit disrupt circadian rhythm.

bodySystems.name: Metabolism & nutrition
bodySystems.spaceflightEffects: PLACEHOLDER: Insulin sensitivity and appetite can change in flight.

missionProfiles.name: ISS (low Earth orbit)
missionProfiles.description: PLACEHOLDER: Near-continuous contact with ground and flight surgeons.

missionProfiles.name: Lunar (Artemis)
missionProfiles.description: PLACEHOLDER: About 1.3 s one-way delay; evacuation to Earth takes days.

missionProfiles.name: Mars transit / surface
missionProfiles.description: PLACEHOLDER: 3–22 min one-way delay; crew must act autonomously.
